newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP launches campaign against alcopops.
newsitem.headline: EP launches campaign against alcopops.

text.p: The European Parliament is launching a campaign against alcopops and designer drinks -- trendily packaged alcoholic drinks which have taken the teenage market by storm across Europe.
"We think it's one of the most cynical marketing exercises ever," British Socialist Euro-MP Eryl McNally told Reuters.
Designer drinks are spirit- or wine-based mixes containing up to 21 percent alcohol.
They come in flashy bottles and cans which appeal to a young market, some with an air of bright sophistication, others shaped like light bulbs or sticks of dynamite.

Alcopops, similarly alluring alcoholic versions of soft drinks like lemonade, often stronger than lager, have stormed ahead since British brewer-to-leisure group Bass launched their market leader Hoopers Hooch 18 months ago.

"Alcopops are available in supermarkets and are so similar to non-alcoholic drinks that cashiers might not spot children buying them. Some haven't even got the word alcoholic on the label," McNally said.

The European Parliament plans to put pressure on the European Commission to propose the EU taxes alcopops and designer drinks at the same rate as spirits and set a code of conduct outlawing marketing tactics which appeal to under-age drinkers.
The parliament also wants a hard-hitting campaign to warn teenagers about the dangers of alcohol abuse.
A spokeswoman for EU Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn said the Commission was concerned by these drinks but could do little other than ensure they were clearly labelled.
She said the Commission had no power to stop the marketing of alcopops, which was in the hands of national governments.
Rodolph Looz, secretary-general of the European Brewers Federation, said he was in favour of a code of conduct which ruled out adverts aimed at children.
Whether or not it was the manufacturers' intention, alcopops were extremely popular with under-age drinkers, an official with the European Confederation of Alcohol Producers said.
